Ordinary GNU floating overloads are out-of-line. Entire current ELF partition is exact reviewed closure or official C glibc overlay, with no ordinary GNU floating from_chars dynamic import. Seven libstdc++ consumers have no loader lookup import; the eighth has one actual dlsym call fixed to __pthread_get_minstack. PDFium static code is confirmed LLVM libc++. Python application has no GNU floating symbol loader route; disposition is bounded to current application code/bytes, not future plugins or arbitrary FFI.

technical_records.affected_feature: CMS encryption to attacker-controlled EC recipient
technical_records.basis: No ELF imports CMS_encrypt/CMS_encrypt_ex, no current Python call site performs CMS envelope encryption, and no openssl CLI exists in the Agent. The installed separate cryptography PKCS7 wrapper also rejects EC recipients before encryption; the recorded synthetic EC-certificate test exercises that real boundary.

The only consumer of the Debian libssl is CPython _ssl, which selects TLS method objects, imports no QUIC methods and performs no dynamic lookup. The reviewed HTTP stack exposes no HTTP/3 or QUIC call site; ordinary TLS negotiation cannot select the separate QUIC transport.

No current application or dependency call site requests AES-GCM-SIV. The system-library path is conventional TLS plus hashing; its actual TLS cipher set contains no GCM-SIV. The separate cryptography implementation is explicitly identified rather than conflated with Debian libcrypto; its installed API definitions are not application call sites.
The same exact TLS-method and caller closure excludes the QUIC CRYPTO-stream processing entry path. This does not claim that a general-purpose QUIC client is unaffected.

The exact current system-library consumers do not select AES-GCM-SIV. Separately, the installed high-level cryptography wrapper rejects tested IV lengths 0,11,13,16 and accepts 12; it has no incremental-update API. These observations are not an upstream fixed-binary claim.
